notes: Main disagreements: (1) phase, mostly during-work vs course-start/general for sample syllabus statements and faculty principles, resolved by whether the passage sets the course rule at course start, states a general principle, or governs work in progress; (2) unit_stance on disclosure units (A require, B permit), resolved to require where the source says students must or should disclose; (3) modality on classification sentences ('constitutes academic dishonesty', 'This includes the unauthorized use of AI'), resolved as informs because they state a classification and do not command, and on 'All other uses are prohibited' (must-not); (4) policy_type on tutor/study-aid permissions (P12 vs P14), the Option 3 and technical-colleague permissions (P12 vs P13, P16 vs P06) and fabrication (P31 vs UNCOVERED), resolved by comparing each with the type definition; (5) splitting: B split disclosure clauses inside Option 1/2 sentences, the 'revise in your own voice' rule and the grammar-check permission, which accounts for most B-only units, all real; A-only units are real statements from the Option 2 sample, one faculty recommendation, and one second sentence in the Provost menu, all kept. Two units from one sentence ('select use types' P05 and 'copy into the syllabus' P09) were kept as separate units and counted as one A-only and one B-only. Stance matched on all five documents (delegates). new_types empty on both sides; the one UNCOVERED unit from B was mapped to P31.
